claims.statement: `launcher.container_run` is the container backend's sequencer: it validates the stack, constructs one `ContainerBackend` (registered under the name `container`, isolation `container`) plus a `LaunchSpec`, and calls the backend capabilities in the order `wire_services` → `provision_tools(FIRST_START)` → `materialize_config` → `seed_auth` → `wire_mcp` → `apply_isolation(BOUNDARY)` → `provision_tools(ATTACH)` → `apply_isolation(EGRESS)`, ending in an `os.execvp` attach.

`ContainerBackend` provisions its volumes BEFORE it materializes config, the reverse of `HostBackend`, because podman's copy-up is what lifts the image's `~/.claude` into the named volume the mount set then delivers; the disagreement is why `ExecutionBackend` is a capability set with deliberately no shared fixed-order driver.

`materialize_config` asserts the two volumes exist (`assert self.config_volume and self.tools_volume`), so the provisioning-before-materializing ordering on this backend is enforced by the caller and named by that assertion; backend-specific state (volume names, mount args, member mounts, pending setups, resolved env-files) lives on the `ContainerBackend` instance rather than in `LaunchSpec`.

`provision_tools(FIRST_START)` calls `volumes._ensure_stack_volumes`, composing both per-stack named volumes in one call (config `harnessed-cfg-<harness>-<stack>` at `~/.claude`, tools `harnessed-tools-<harness>-<stack>` at `~/.local`, plus the shared `harnessed-dl-cache`), so an unchanged stack pays nothing and a changed stack reinstalls with no `podman build` at all.

The volume-composition invariant is: podman copy-up lifts the image's `~/.claude` into the volume, then the profile is layered on top with `cp -a src/. dst/` which MERGES rather than replaces — never mount a profile directory over a config subtree. That shadowing is the bug the composed volume replaced: the old per-subdir `:ro` bind-mounts hid 70 of 75 skills (including all 34 `gsd-*`) because `synclinks._fan_into` creates skills/commands/rules unconditionally and the mount gate was existence, not non-emptiness.

The volume-populate throwaway container must use the same `paths.USERNS_ARG` as the pod: a volume first populated under the default userns is unreadable by the agent (uid 1000 reads files as owner 999 and every write EACCESes). Volumes are identified by label (`harnessed.role`/`harnessed.stack`/`harnessed.harness`), never by parsing the name, because a stack name may contain the same hyphens the name format uses.

The container fingerprint gate is the host stack fingerprint PLUS the image id, forced by copy-up running exactly once per volume (after that, volume content wins and image updates are invisible). When the fingerprint moves, the config volume is discarded (`fresh=not unchanged`) because composition is only additive; the TOOLS volume is kept since `mise use -g` is declarative. The stamp is written only after installs succeed.

`volumes._merged_settings_text` deep-merges the profile's `settings.json` OVER the volume's install-written one instead of copying, because `_ensure_config_volume` runs on every launch while installs run only when the fingerprint moved — a plain copy dropped every install-written key on every relaunch after the first. A failed volume read is treated as absent, not empty, and the merged body is passed by env (`HARNESSED_SETTINGS_JSON`) and written with `printf %s`, never interpolated into the `-c` string.

`materialize_config` composes one ORDERED mount block (mcp.json, the two volumes, per-harness identity files, rw history dirs, the firewall script, the path-mirroring mount, then claude.json stub, keyring, mcp-auth store, omp agent dir + its mcp.json shadow + config.yml shadow, ccstatusline, corp CA, persist mounts, credential forwarding, and AWS SSO env). The order is load-bearing; a known imprecision (tracked as harnessed-0tk.1.1) is that several credential mounts are composed here rather than in `seed_auth`, and the block is not split because the suite runs no `podman run`.

`_omp_mcp_seed_mount` is emitted immediately after `_omp_agent_mount`, because it shadows the dir mount's own `mcp.json`: a per-instance file equal to the host's mcp.json plus a `hatago` HTTP entry, mounted `:ro` over `~/.omp/agent/mcp.json`, so omp (which has no `--mcp-config` flag) reaches the hub without mutating the shared host file. omp's image bakes `~/.omp/{plugins,natives}` and not `agent/`, so the rw dir mount shadows nothing.

`seed_auth` resolves launch-time secrets via `_resolve_launch_secrets` and appends the Claude credential mount LAST; whether it is needed at all depends on a `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` that may arrive via `--env-file`, which is why the mount cannot be composed one step earlier. `seed_auth` also runs after every aborting check in `materialize_config` so an early exit cannot strand resolved secrets on disk.

`_claude_creds_seed_mount` is the legacy fallback: a per-instance rw copy of the host's `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, re-seeded only when the existing copy's access token has passed `expiresAt` (so a token the container itself refreshed is never clobbered). A configured `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` supersedes it entirely — nothing is mounted in that case — and the mount is rw because a ro mount blocks Claude Code's in-container token refresh.

`mounts._env_files_value` walks the resolved `--env-file`s in order and keeps the LAST assignment, matching podman's last-wins; `_resolve_launch_secrets` orders the files global → project precisely so project overrides global. An explicit empty string is a real answer distinct from `None` ("declared, and turned off") — returning on the first hit would let a global token mask a project-level `VAR=` written to disable it. `_claude_oauth_token_configured` has the same shape for the same reason.

`_claude_oauth_token_args` forwards the host-env token as a bare `-e NAME` (podman reads the value from its own env, keeping the secret off `ps`), but the env-file route wins: because podman's `-e` beats `--env-file`, the forward is WITHHELD whenever any env-file assigns the variable, empty included — a non-empty assignment makes it redundant, and an empty one is how a source turns the token off.

Every env-file handed to podman is a generated mode-0600 temp (the user's own `.env` is copied and normalized, never passed directly), and `apply_isolation(BOUNDARY)` unlinks them in a `finally` as soon as podman has ingested them — resolved secret values must not linger on disk, on success or failure.

For an `isolated_auth` claude stack, three suppressions make the wrong-account guard hold: `_claude_isolated_auth_mount` seeds the stack's own per-instance credentials file (as `{}`, never re-seeded, never expiry-checked), `_strip_var_from_env_files` deletes `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` from the already-resolved env-files (because `--env-file` is passed unconditionally), and `_build_pod_args` elides the `-e` forward. All three are gated on the harness being claude, since omp authenticates from the same variable.

The isolated-auth login store is a host file rather than a path in the config volume, because `_ensure_config_volume` DESTROYS the volume whenever the profile fingerprint changes — the volume's own "safe to destroy: credentials are bind-mounted over it and live on the host" invariant is exactly what the isolated-auth store relies on.

Private-key (`ssh_keys:`) forwarding is honoured only from the user's own overlay catalog (`stack_from_overlay`), never from a shared repo-catalog stack; the full `forward_git_credentials` bundle forwards the SSH signing/auth agent, the non-secret GPG surface (never `private-keys-v1.d/`), YubiKey USB passthrough (Linux only), git identity config, gh's hosts.yml/config.yml `:ro`, and the non-secret `~/.ssh` surface plus opted-in private keys file-by-file — never a blanket `~/.ssh` mount. Without the opt-in, `_ssh_agent_auto_forward_args` still auto-forwards the live agent socket and ro git config, safe because the socket exposes no key material.

`wire_mcp` writes a PER-INSTANCE hatago config (`prof/.instances/<inst>/hatago.config.json`) via `emit.write_hatago_config`, pinning each stdio child's cwd to the mirrored project path because the committed profile config is project-agnostic; it then derives `self.member_mounts` as `_without_userns(self.mount_args)` plus the hatago config `:ro` plus `_setup_script_mounts`. `_without_userns` filters on the `--userns` FLAG, not a literal value, because podman rejects `--userns` on a pod member.

`apply_isolation(BOUNDARY)` is both the isolation boundary and the delivery mechanism: the single `podman run` is the only way mounts and env cross it, which is why the env assembly lives there rather than in `materialize_config`, and why the setup env is resolved there (a `setup.config` item may prompt and must do so before the container starts).

The pod is created with `paths.USERNS_ARG` = `--userns=keep-id:uid=1000,gid=1000`, pinned to the image uid rather than bare `keep-id` so the container's uid-1000 process IS the invoking host user whatever their host uid (bare keep-id made bind-mount writes depend on the host uid happening to be 1000). `--hostname` is set explicitly on the pod via `paths.container_hostname` because podman otherwise derives it from the pod name, which crun rejects past HOST_NAME_MAX.

The pod publishes mcp-remote's OAuth callback port as `-p 127.0.0.1:<port>:<port>` (loopback-bound, never unqualified) and pairs it with `--network pasta:--host-lo-to-ns-lo` as ONE list (`_mcp_remote_pod_args`) — the publish alone is inert because mcp-remote binds 127.0.0.1 unconditionally and rootless pasta forwards published ports to the namespace's public address. An explicit `HARNESSED_NET` wins with a note; a taken or sub-1024 port is skipped, not fatal; no pin means no publish.

`apply_isolation(BOUNDARY)` orders `-e` flags by precedence: `--env-file`s first, then recipe `env:` FIRST (catalog-authored, must not be able to clobber harnessed-owned values), then the token forward, then the folder-env contract (`harnessed_env`), the setup env, `MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS`, and `HATAGO_TRANSPORT` last. Podman applies `-e` left-to-right so the LAST wins, and this matches host mode — reversing the two silently inverts precedence between backends.

Env is set on the CONTAINER rather than on one exec so hooks and later `podman exec` see what the setup script saw: `harnessed_env` (folder-env contract), `_container_setup_env` (resolved host-side because a `setup.config` item may prompt before the container starts), and `MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS` (setup scripts run as `podman exec … bash <script>`, neither login nor interactive, so mise would otherwise refuse the project's config).

The container's image command is `bash -c 'exec /usr/local/bin/harnessed-start 2>/dev/null || exec sleep infinity'` — a graceful fallback on older images. `harnessed-start` starts the hatago hub in the background only when a config was mounted AND `HATAGO_TRANSPORT=http` (under stdio a background hub would spawn a second copy of every stdio child, contending for one lockfile and one callback port), then `exec sleep infinity`, preserving the invariant that only an interactive attach owns a real pts.

The attach phase runs in order: `_install_corp_proxy_ca_in_container` (local-only, no network), `provision_tools(ATTACH)` (podman exec of each setup script), then `apply_isolation(EGRESS)` — a first-run setup is exactly the step that downloads things, so egress closes after it. `_pending_setup_scripts` deliberately ignores `setup.condition` (a condition is a first-run gate, so gating on it makes a script fresh-project-only); scripts are idempotent and run every launch to converge. `setup.confirm` requires an explicit yes, and no TTY means SKIP, never run.

The egress firewall is fail-closed at the script layer: `egress-firewall.sh` wraps every must-succeed iptables call in `require` (exit 1 with a FATAL message rather than report success), runs `set -uo pipefail` WITHOUT `-e` so the per-domain resolution loop may fail per host, and finally verifies its own end state by checking `iptables -S OUTPUT` for `-P OUTPUT DROP` before printing "Egress active".

Before the fix, the script's `set -uo pipefail` without `-e` plus a closing `exit 0` meant 43 consecutive "Permission denied" iptables failures still printed "[firewall] Egress active" and exited 0, so the launcher's fail-closed guard never fired and every container ran with unrestricted egress — the reason `require` and the self-verification now exist.

The launcher independently verifies the firewall: `_apply_firewall` refuses to continue on a non-zero exit from the script, then calls `_firewall_policy_is_drop`, which reads `iptables -S OUTPUT` back out of the pod's netns and returns True only for an explicit `-P OUTPUT DROP` line. Anything unreadable is False, so "cannot prove it is confined" and "is not confined" reach the same fail-closed branch; both failures name `NO_FIREWALL=true` as the deliberate opt-out and exit 1.

On any failure in the EGRESS phase the pod is torn down before re-raising, and the handler catches `BaseException` — not `typer.Exit` — because `_bounded` catches only `TimeoutExpired`, so an `OSError` from `subprocess.run` (podman missing, permission denied) would skip a narrower handler and leave exactly the unconfined container this exists to prevent; Ctrl-C belongs here too. Nothing is swallowed: every path re-raises.

The firewall is installed and verified by a THROWAWAY container (`_firewall_runner_argv`: `podman run --rm --cap-add NET_ADMIN --user root`, joined to the pod's netns), never by exec-ing into the agent: installing iptables rules needs CAP_NET_ADMIN and the agent container must never hold it, or the confined process could flush the rules that confine it. `--user root` is required because NET_ADMIN in the bounding set is not enough for the unprivileged image user to call iptables.

`wire_services` is called BEFORE the re-attach branch, deliberately: a long-lived agent container outlives its sidecars, and when the call sat on the create path only, every subsequent launch took the attach branch and never looked at services again — a sidecar that died stayed dead for the life of the container. `_ensure_services` is idempotent per referenced service (skip a running container whose create-time config hash matches, recreate a drifted one), and a healthcheck that never passes aborts the launch.

The container path never assembles — its profile was assembled back at `harnessed build` — so anything `assemble()` guards must be re-checked at launch. Today that is `_validate_direct_servers(launch_servers, harness)`: an image built before a recipe gained `direct:` would otherwise reach launch with servers the harness never sees (excluded from hatago's config by `direct`, and only claude's MCP config is emitted per stack), leaving an omp or codex stack silently toolless.

`launcher._attach` execs `podman exec -it -e TERM=xterm-256color -w <start_dir> <inst> bash -l -c <shell_cmd>` where `shell_cmd` is `mise_init && init_prologue && [keyring_init] && tail`. Default (no `--rm`) it calls `os.execvp(rt, exec_argv)` with the argv as a vector (nothing word-split or glob-expanded), replacing the process and handing the TTY to the container natively; under `--rm` the exec runs as a child so a bounded `finally` can reap the pod when the session exits.

The attach command is derived per harness in `attachcmd.py` (pure derivation, nothing spawns): claude gets `claude --mcp-config '<mcp_cfg>'` with ` --strict-mcp-config` by default (so the stack's `.mcp.json` is the only MCP source; `--no-strict-mcp-config` empties it), omp gets a `--session-dir` pin, opencode gets `--agent <name>` only when a persona was baked (via the same `emit.opencode_agent_name` that keyed it), and antigravity (`agy`) / codex get fixed commands.

`_omp_attach_cmd` recomputes omp's per-folder session-dir key against the HOST home and pins it with `--session-dir`, because in the pod `$HOME` is `/home/harnessed` while the agent's cwd is the mirrored host path — outside the pod's home — so omp escapes the key and writes to a folder the host never reads, and `/resume` in the pod reported "No sessions in current folder". The dir is fixed at attach time; no `--profile` is used, since that would isolate auth/sessions into a store that ignores the bind-mounted `~/.omp/agent`.

`_authorize_mcp_remote_servers` runs after the pod is up (the callback publish and store mount both come from it) and before the harness attaches, because mcp-remote only reveals it needs a browser after hatago has spawned it, on a grandchild's stderr the harness discards. `_mcp_remote_pending_auth` computes the exact token path (`<store>/mcp-remote-<version>/<sha256(server_url)>_tokens.json`, the version read back out of the recipe's own argv); an expired token is deliberately not pending. The consent runs IN the container, and the completion signal is a parseable non-empty JSON token file — not existence, since mcp-remote writes with a plain `writeFile` and no atomic rename.

`_wait_hatago` is skipped when `hub_transport` is `stdio` (the harness spawns the hub at attach) and when every server is direct (`emit.hub_is_needed` false) — probing for a hub that was deliberately never started would wait out the timeout and report a degraded hub, turning correct configuration into a red herring and, headless, into a hard exit. In headless mode a dead hub IS a hard `typer.Exit(1)`, and the SUCCESS line names the hub's whereabouts rather than a fixed string.

`--fresh` tears the pod down and additionally wipes the persisted agy keyring (`_keyring_fresh_wipe`) and an isolated-auth stack's own login (`_isolated_auth_fresh_wipe`) — those two deliberately survive a normal recreate, so `--fresh` is the only way back to a logged-out agent. `HARNESSED_HEADLESS=true` disables the re-attach branch and every interactive prompt; a stopped leftover from a prior non-ephemeral session is removed and recreated because a same-name `pod create` would fail.

Every podman call in the launch goes through `proc._bounded` with a deadline sized by what the command does (30 s read-only metadata, 120 s state changes and execs, 10 s readiness probes), turning a hung podman into "failed" rather than "hangs"; the interactive session and the browser consent are deliberately unbounded, while the teardown beside them is bounded.

The pytest suite runs no real podman, so the container path's guarantees are pinned by unit tests over the pure derivations (mount-block order, `_env_files_value` last-wins and empty-vs-None, the withheld token forward, `_strip_var_from_env_files`, hub/mcp-config consistency, the attach commands, the firewall runner argv and the strict DROP line match, the volume label scheme and the fingerprint's image-id component). The podman-gated live layer behind `HARNESSED_PODMAN=1` and the capability test (which drives `container-run --fresh` headlessly and host-derives the instance name) are what exercise a real launch.

`backend.ExecutionBackend` names exactly the six capabilities of BACKENDS.md §3 — materialize config, provision tools, wire MCP, seed auth, wire services, apply isolation — as abstract methods, alongside `name` and `isolation` ClassVars (`isolation` a declared capability, not an enum the code branches on). Two of the six, `provision_tools` and `apply_isolation`, carry a phase argument (`FIRST_START`/`ATTACH` and `BOUNDARY`/`EGRESS`) because each has two moments on BOTH existing backends and cannot collapse into one call on either.

The container and host sequencers are deliberately NOT symmetric, and the asymmetry is the design: the container provisions before materializing (copy-up must populate the volume the mounts reference), assembles env inside `apply_isolation(BOUNDARY)` (the one `podman run` is the only way env crosses), and enforces real isolation; the host materializes before provisioning under the home lock, assembles env onto `os.environ`, and declares isolation `none` while still calling both `apply_isolation` phases. Three things must hold identically on both, and do: credentials are delivered by reference (never replicated), the env winners are the same (recipe `env:` underneath, harnessed-owned folder-env and secrets above), and the same `_merge_host_claude_settings` fold of the host's live preferences is applied to the profile before the backend sees it.

The corporate proxy CA crosses the boundary in two steps: `_corp_proxy_ca_mount_args` bind-mounts the cert `:ro` at `/run/corp-proxy-ca.crt` in the mount block, and after the container starts `_install_corp_proxy_ca_in_container` execs as root inside it to copy the cert into `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` and run `update-ca-certificates`. It runs FIRST among the post-start steps — local-only, needing no network — so it precedes `provision_tools(ATTACH)` and `apply_isolation(EGRESS)` and every post-start container mutation happens on the unconfined side of the firewall.
